articles.title: PlayStation State Of Play September 2026: Start Time, How To Watch, And What To Expect
articles.summary: Just when you thought there would be a post-Gamescom break for video game livestreams, Sony dropped notice that the State of Play broadcast was returning with two back-to-back broadcasts.
body: As usual, State of Play will be streamed live on Sony’s YouTube and Twitch channels.

The first State of Play broadcast will offer updates and announcements from PlayStation Studios and third-party partners. The livestream will close out with an extended look at Final Fantasy 7 Revelation, and immediately after, it'll be followed by a new episode of State of Play Japan. Hosted by Yuki Kaji, State of Play Japan will be focused entirely on upcoming games from game studios in Japan and Asia, so expect trailers and gameplay aplenty.

September alone is packed with new releases, including the PS5-exclusive Marvel's Wolverine alongside Control Resonant, NBA 2K27, The Blood of Dawnwalker, and Onimusha: Way of the Sword, so new trailers for those games wouldn't be unlikely. Looking ahead to October, there are even more high-profile releases like Hellraiser: Revival, Castlevania: Belmont's Curse, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, and Final Fantasy Resonance, just to name a few. And in November?

articles.title: Following Nintendo's example, Sony and Microsoft argue they have no obligation to pass tariff refunds onto customers
articles.summary: Lawyers representing Sony and Microsoft have argued, in two separate lawsuits, that the platform holders are not obligated to pass tariff refunds back to consumers. Sony and Microsoft have had to raise prices of their PlayStation and Xbox consoles in 2025 in response to US-imposed tariffs.
body: Both Sony and Microsoft will receive refunds, but consumers who paid higher prices for their products as a result of the tariffs will not be compensated. As reported by Game File, the two companies are being sued separately by affected consumers who say they should receive refunds.
In Sony's case, brought against it by a group of players in California, the company used a familiar line of argument that essentially said consumers got what they paid for.

"Paying fair market price for voluntarily purchased consumer goods is not a legally cognisable injury in fact," Sony argued in a legal motion. The company is seeking to dismiss the suit early before it could turn into a class-action lawsuit.
Microsoft's case was initiated by one individual in Washington State, who is likewise seeking a refund. Once again, the company's argument against the suit is familiar.
points: Lawyers representing Sony and Microsoft have argued, in two separate lawsuits, that the platform holders are not obligated to pass tariff refunds back to consumers.
Sony and Microsoft have had to raise prices of their PlayStation and Xbox consoles in 2025 in response to US-imposed tariffs.
Both Sony and Microsoft will receive refunds, but consumers who paid higher prices for their products as a result of the tariffs will not be compensated.
As reported by Game File, the two companies are being sued separately by affected consumers who say they should receive refunds.

articles.title: Clint Eastwood's Forgotten Western That Redefined His Career Is Officially Free to Watch on YouTube
articles.summary: More than 60 years since their release, all three movies in Clint Eastwood’s “The Man with No Name Trilogy” remain classics. 1964’s A Fistful of Dollars, 1965’s For a Few Dollars More, and 1996’s The Good, the Bad and the Ugly are all Italian-made films by director Sergio Leone set in the American…
body: They are so successful that they overshadow Eastwood’s very next Western after completing the trilogy, a movie that is every bit as good as the Man with No Name movies. It’s also a film that's entirely free to stream on YouTube.

Hang ‘Em High is a 1968 Western directed by Ted Post, written by Leonard Freeman and Mel Goldberg, and produced by Eastwood himself. The Man with No Name movies made Eastwood a star, so he used some of that clout to begin to exercise his muscle as a filmmaker. He personally chose Post, who he worked with on the TV show Rawhide (1959), to direct, and Eastwood also made script changes to Hang ‘Em High to flesh out his character. Eastwood didn’t direct a movie himself until a few years later, but Hang ‘Em High is a milestone on his path to becoming one of America’s great directors.

articles.title: Dragon Ball Super Shares Release Date and Spectacular Trailer Full of New Details
articles.summary: The wait is over: the remake of the Dragon Ball Super anime, Dragon Ball Super: Beerus, finally has a release date. The long-awaited next entry in the Dragon Ball franchise will debut on Fuji TV on Oct. 11. Fans in the US will be able to catch a world-premiere screening of the first episode on Oct.
body: A new "super surge trailer" accompanied the announcement, giving Dragon Ball fans the first extensive look at what the remake will look like. It's safe to say that Toei Animation did not disappoint: The trailer showcases the high-quality visuals everybody expected from this remake, and also sheds light on how long the anime will be and which arcs it will cover.

The trailer also revealed the anime's opening and ending themes: "Onogami" by Megatera - Zero and "Kan Peki No Peki" by VK Blanka. While fans will miss the iconic opening theme of the original anime, "Chosetsu Dynamic!", the new songs from these young Japanese artists convey the same sense of energy and excitement, and overall contribute to giving Dragon Ball Super: Beerus a fresh vibe.

In terms of differences, fans noticed that in the trailer scenes showing Goku's battle against Frieza, the protagonist uses his Super Saiyan God form before transforming into Super Saiyan Blue, a detail that was missing from the Resurrection 'F' movie. It may not seem like much, but true Dragon Ball fans live and die for these small details, so this makes the expectations around Dragon Ball Super: Beerus even higher.

articles.title: 11 Best MAPPA Anime That Aren’t 'Jujutsu Kaisen' or 'Chainsaw Man'
articles.summary: It's impossible to escape the monolithic shadow of Studio MAPPA when looking at today’s anime landscape. For a majority of fans, the name is synonymous with a specific flavor of modern blockbuster.
body: Founded in 2011 by Madhouse co-founder and industry rebel Masao Maruyama, the studio was originally envisioned as an artistic sanctuary. Long before it was trusted to helm storied projects like Attack on Titan and Vinland Saga, MAPPA was built as a boutique haven where legendary directors could escape the shackles of corporate production committees and build personal passion projects that nobody else would fund. Over the years, that indie-darling DNA has collided with its rapid ascension in the industry, creating a unique identity that balances mainstream domination with a lingering desire to swing for the fences.

To truly appreciate MAPPA’s place in anime, you have to look past the cursed energy and the contracts. When you strip away its flagship projects, what’s left is a stunningly diverse lineup of historical dramas, subversive idol parodies, and bizarre passion projects that were once deemed unadaptable. From its very first jazz-infused steps to its most recent love letter to the grueling art of animation, here are the 11 best MAPPA anime that prove there’s more to the studio's soul than blockbuster adaptations.

articles.title: 31 Years Later, the Smartest 'Calvin and Hobbes' Character Still Doesn't Get the Recognition They Deserve
articles.summary: Every once in a while, some fan artist draws a continuation or sequel to Calvin and Hobbes, which is frequently themed around the idea of an adult Calvin passing Hobbes on to his own child.
body: Hobbes and Bacon is probably the best example of what's become an oddly persistent trope in Calvin and Hobbes fan lore: Calvin growing up to marry Susie. It's understandable how someone might have that reading. Susie is Calvin's only consistent peer throughout the strip's original run. If Calvin's going to marry any canon character, she's really the only option on the board. It's simultaneously a strange choice, though, as the strip usually treats Susie and Calvin like oil and water.

There are exceptions, such as the Valentine's Day arc from 1986, and that can be chalked up to the same early installment weirdness that gave us Calvin's Uncle Max. Otherwise, Susie is in Calvin and Hobbes to serve as Calvin's foil: well-adjusted vs. Calvin's maladjusted, a good student vs. a scholastic misfit, order vs. chaos. While there are occasional hints that Calvin and Susie might have a crush on one another, it's still difficult to believe they could ever stay in the same room long enough to have a civil conversation, let alone a kid.

articles.title: Resident Evil's Zach Cregger Admits He Was 'Naive' to Assume Fans Would Approve of Him Avoiding a Direct Adaptation of the Games
articles.summary: Zach Cregger admitted that he was “naive” to think his less-direct approach to adapting Resident Evil would be universally well-received by fans after deliberately choosing to avoid retelling the story exactly as it unfolds in the games.
body: Cregger’s Resident Evil movie follows Bryan (Austin Abrams), a medical courier who gets caught up in the madness of the Raccoon City Incident. The writer/director confirmed previously that this film takes place in parallel to the events of Resident Evil 2 and that it focuses more on what it feels like as a player to navigate through zombie-filled corridors and sneak around Lickers… but not everyone was anticipating an original story told within the continuity of Capcom’s beloved horror game franchise.

Instead, a slew of fans have lashed out at Cregger for not directly adapting an existing game in the series, with many arguing that, without characters like Leon, Ada, and Jill, this isn’t really a Resident Evil movie at all.
IGN’s Tom Jorgensen got the chance to sit down with Cregger to ask him about his feelings on this particular topic — and his response was strikingly self-aware.

articles.title: Alienware Just Released the World's First 39" 5K Monitor With RGB Stripe Tandem OLED Technology
articles.summary: Earlier this year, Dell announced the "world's first 39" 5K monitor with RGB stripe tandem OLED technology." You can finally get your hands on one. The new Alienware AW3926QW has just been listed at Dell for $1,099.99 with free delivery (10% less if you have a verified student account).
body: The Alienware AW3926QW has no lack of features that make it stand out from the crowd, but perhaps its most impressive technology is the RGB stripe tandem OLED panel. Tandem OLED stacks multiple OLED layers on top of each other instead of a single layer. Tandem OLED is better than other OLED panels because: 1) it's much brighter (the AW3926QW in particular has a very impressive 1,300 nits of peak brightness) and 2) it's less prone to burn-in.

The AW3926QW doubles down on this with new RGB stripe technology. Whereas traditional tandem OLEDs use white pixels, RGB stripe tandem OLED breaks the color down further into vertically aligned red, green, and blue pixels. This reduces color fringing and in turn significantly improves text clarity. It goes without saying that there are obvious benefits here for both gaming and productivity purposes alike.

articles.title: CD Projekt Red Is Still Raking In The Cash As We Wait For The Witcher 4
articles.summary: CD Projekt Red has released its latest earnings report for the first half of 2026, and in short, it was a banger of a period for the company, and things are only expected to improve with many big-name releases on the horizon.
body: For the January-July period, CD Projekt Red generated 435 million PLN ($116.4 million USD) in revenue, which was up 23% year-over-year. Additionally, the company posted a net profit of 249 million PLN ($66.6 million USD), which was up 37% year-over-year. Total net profitability for the company was a very impressive 57%.

Management said in its report that these strong results were driven in part by "strong sales" of The Witcher and Cyberpunk games. Additionally, CD Projekt said it benefitted nicely from licensing revenue, a category that is becoming more and more important to the company.

The company specifically called out licensing deals that Cyberpunk 2077 had with games like Wuthering Waves and Apex Legends this year. Additionally, the company pointed out how well Cyberpunk TCG did on Kickstarter.

It would appear that CD Projekt's revenues are only set to grow further in the time ahead. That's because the studio has a lot of big games and content on tap, including The Witcher 3 Remastered this year, The Witcher 3's Songs of the Past expansion in 2027, and then The Witcher 4 in 2028.

articles.title: A Real-Life Romance (And The Love Of Fans) Fueled A Classic NES Remake
articles.summary: With headlines dominated by stories of buyouts, layoffs, employee mistreatment, and crunch, it's easy to think that game development is a constant parade of misery and strife.
body: The Battle of Olympus is a side-scrolling action-RPG released in 1988 by Broderbund for the NES. The visuals and gameplay take a lot of cues from Zelda II, though with a Greek mythology-inspired story and setting and a pretty solid challenge level throughout. It's been described as "a hidden gem" of the NES library many times, often overshadowed by similar titles, but beloved by those who enjoyed it.

Notably, The Battle of Olympus was developed in Japan by a very small developer named Infinity. How small? Well, the game's credits list a whopping three different people--Yukio Horimoto, Reiko Oshida, and Kazuo Sawa. Yukio and Reiko were the two main collaborators, with Yukio handling programming, Reiko on art design, and the pair working together on the game's story. As it turns out, the project would lead the two to discover their connection to each other, and they would marry soon after--making it very fitting that The Battle of Olympus's Japanese subtitle is "The Legend of Love."

articles.title: Kingdom Hearts almost led to Disney making its own version of Super Smash Bros, former dev says
articles.summary: Kingdom Hearts bashing together a bunch of Disney's best toys (and being quite successful in the process) led the Mouse House to briefly begin work on a crossover fighting game in the style of Super Smash Bros.
body: That's according to Ken Christiansen, a former Disney Interactive concept artist who also had credits on the very first Kingdom Hearts game. In an interview with Time Extension, the developer said Kingdom Hearts' world-hopping shenanigans opened Disney's eyes to a whole universe of potential crossover projects.

The development of the original Kingdom Hearts game was apparently a little difficult "because Disney was so reluctant to have that possibility of crossing over The Lion King into The Little Mermaid world," Christiansen recalled.

Disney supposedly "couldn't get over" seeing its most popular characters run into each other constantly, and the company's hesitance meant there was "just a little bit of butting heads" during production, even if most of the developers "thought it was the greatest idea in the world."

Regardless of how unexcited certain Disney executives were about Square Enix 's still-whacky series, it was a pretty major success. The first Kingdom Hearts became one of the PlayStation 2's best-selling games and, as you can imagine, put dollar signs in the eyes of company higher ups.

articles.title: Iconic Banjo-Kazooie composer is more hopeful about a sequel these days, but knows "like three companies" have already been turned down
articles.summary: Grant Kirkhope - the iconic video game composer behind the Donkey Kong Rap and the Banjo-Kazooie games - thinks a potential Banjo-Threeie is slightly more likely now.
body: Almost three decades have passed since Banjo-Kazooie's last mainline platformer flapped onto the N64 and it's been almost 20 years since Banjo-Kazooie: Nuts and Bolts flopped onto the Xbox 360, but it's never too late for another adventure with the bird and bear.

Speaking to FRVR, Kirkhope explained that he used to feel there was "zero chance of another Banjo-Kazooie game." Nowadays, that sentiment's been upgraded to a "slight chance" because he thinks Rare's updated leadership could be more receptive to an outside developer spearheading a threequel.

"Rare just typically say no to everything," the composer explained. "I've known people present cartoons to them, all sorts of ideas, and they just say no to everything." But since former studio head Craig Duncan stepped down from his role at Xbox Game Studios, Kirkhope reckons Rare might be "a little bit different right now" and "a bit more open to discussion."
